solution:
<explanation>A combines residual signal propagation, three normalization blocks, and LeakyReLU with substantial Adam training progress. B’s faster momentum SGD remains disadvantaged by its deep plain SiLU stack and fewer normalization blocks; the larger nominal progress estimate does not resolve those bottlenecks. C adds normalization but reduces SGD’s learning rate thirtyfold, leaving much less fitting progress. <cited>K1006,K1012,K1019,K1039</cited></explanation>
<answer>A</answer>
comment: A’s normalized residual LeakyReLU stack with Adam was the stronger recipe than either deep plain SiLU stack with momentum SGD. K1039 supported caution about smooth activations under SGD on MSE, while K1006 supported normalization as a conditional preference. K1019 and K1012 prevented treating B’s larger calibrated progress estimate as decisive across different architectures. C’s thirtyfold lower SGD rate further weakened its prospects despite its extra normalization block. The gold validates this bundled prediction, not an isolated activation, residual, or optimizer effect. No new tested general rule follows from this case.
